 Sam Coffey leads the U.S. contingent on Matchday 3, with several other American players set to feature across Europe.
 Matt McNulty Roddy Cons twitter Digital sports journalist About the author Scottish sports journalist and content creator. After running his own soccer-related projects, in 2022 he joined Diario AS, where he mainly reports on the biggest news from around Europe’s leading soccer clubs, Liga MX and MLS, and covers live games in a not-too-serious tone. Likes to mix things up by dipping into the world of American sports. Update: Oct 29th, 2026 11:05 EDT 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google The UEFA Women’s Champions League continues Thursday, Oct. 29, with plenty of American involvement as Matchday 3 of the league phase concludes.
 On Wednesday, Emily Fox (Arsenal), Alyssa Thompson and Naomi Girma (both Chelsea), Lily Yohannes and Korbin Shrader (both Lyon), Maya Doms (Roma) and Camille Lafaix (Oud-Heverlee Leuven) were all in action. Several more U.S. players could take the field in Thursday’s fixtures.
 Manchester City vs. Paris Saint-Germain
 Kick-off: 3:00 p.m. ET | Watch: Paramount+
 U.S. women’s national team midfielder Sam Coffey, who has 46 caps for the Stars and Stripes, is the highest-profile American involved in Thursday’s games.
 After four years with Portland Thorns in the NWSL, the New York native joined Manchester City in January 2026 , helping the Sky Blues win the Women’s Super League in England just a few months later.
 Sam Coffey signed a 3.5-year deal with Manchester City after an $875K transfer from the Portland Thorns ✍️
But the parking tickets are STILL following her 🚗😅 pic.twitter.com/ASNnACetFl 
— TNT Sports U.S. (@TNTSportsUS) October 13, 2026 
 HB Køge vs. Barcelona
 Kick-off: 3:00 p.m. ET | Watch: Paramount+
 Goalkeeper Tyler McCarney could well be in the Barcelona squad for this one, although her chances of getting any playing time in Denmark are next to none.
 HB Køge , the Danish champions, are much more intriguing from an American perspective.
 In May 2025, Angie and Chris Long , majority owners of NWSL club Kansas City Current , acquired HB Køge Women through their investment company, Ballard Capital.
 The deal brought the Danish club under the same majority ownership as the Current , creating an opportunity to share expertise and develop talent across the two clubs.
 Barcelona have been firing on all cylinders in Europe this season ⚽️
A Champions League goal-fest 𝙘𝙤𝙪𝙡𝙙 be on the cards against HB Køge 🫨 pic.twitter.com/0WSV6Gb1K0 
— LiveScore (@livescore) October 29, 2026 
 Defender Sydney Jones joined HB Køge in May 2026 from Kansas City Current II, the NWSL club’s reserve side. Midfielder Catherine Paulson arrived from Bay FC in March 2026.
 Goalkeeper Lauren Kozal, defender Emma Flick and forward Macy Schultz complete the five-player American contingent.
 While not included in the Champions League squad , Samantha Williams is back in action domestically after a long-term injury, adding another American connection to the team.
 Paris FC vs. BK Häcken
 Kick-off: 1:45 p.m. ET | Watch: Paramount+
 Swedish champions BK Häcken haven’t gone quite as big on Americans, but they still have two on their roster.
 Florida-born midfielder/forward Tabby Tindell , who has played her entire career in Sweden, joined the club in 2024, while defensive midfielder Laney Egbuka , who grew up in Ohio, is in her first year with the team.
